- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7–14 day average.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by > 2% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misreads momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 14-day high if sentiment remains positive.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
